answers: I have just finished my homework.
I've just done my homework.
He has already eaten lunch.
He's already had lunch.
The bus has just left.
The bus just left.
questions.explanation: 현재완료: 막 떠나서 지금도 없음 강조

answers: She has lost a lot of weight.
She's lost so much weight.
I have lost my keys.
I've lost my keys.
questions.explanation: 현재완료는 과거 사건이 현재에 영향을 줄 때 사용

answers: Have you ever tried Thai food?
Have you ever eaten Thai food?

questions.korean: 나는 한 번도 패러글라이딩을 해본 적이 없어.
answers: I have never tried paragliding.
I've never gone paragliding.
Have you had this kind of food before?
Have you tried this type of food before?
She has seen a musical before.
She has been to a musical.
questions.explanation: have been to = ~에 가본 적 있다

questions.korean: 나는 그런 실수를 한 번도 한 적이 없어.
answers: I have never made such a mistake.
I've never done anything like that.
questions.hint: have never + made + such a mistake

answers: I have been a vegetarian for five years.
I've been eating vegetarian for five years.
He has been sick since last Tuesday.
He's been ill since Tuesday.
questions.explanation: since = 특정 시점부터, for = 기간 동안

answers: They have been running this company since 2015.
They've been managing this company since 2015.
We have been friends since college.
We've been close since our college days.

questions.korean: 그녀는 얼마나 오랫동안 영어를 가르쳐 왔어?
answers: How long has she been teaching English?
How long has she taught English?
The news is updated every day.
The news gets updated daily.
The bill was passed by the National Assembly.
The bill was approved by Congress.
The report must be submitted by tomorrow.
The report needs to be turned in by tomorrow.

questions.korean: 그 영화는 유명한 소설을 원작으로 만들어졌어.
answers: The movie was based on a famous novel.
The film was adapted from a famous novel.
The building is being repaired now.
The building is under repair.
That's the man whose car broke down.
That's the guy whose car stopped working.
She is the person whom I talked about.
She is the person I mentioned.
questions.explanation: 구어체에서는 whom 대신 who 또는 생략

questions.korean: 나는 아버지가 유명한 작가인 친구가 있어.
answers: I have a friend whose father is a famous writer.
I know someone whose dad is a famous author.

questions.korean: 그녀가 나한테 소개해준 남자가 실제로 나의 상사야.
answers: The man whom she introduced to me is actually my boss.
The man she introduced me to is actually my boss.

questions.korean: 그건 내가 전혀 기대하지 않았던 결과야.
answers: That's a result that I didn't expect at all.
That's not what I expected at all.
questions.explanation: not what I expected = 내가 기대한 것이 아닌

answers: This is the place where we first met.
This is where we first met.
2020 was the year when the pandemic started.
2020 was when the pandemic began.
That's the reason why I quit.
That's why I quit.
This is the place where we'll have the party.
This is where we're going to hold the party.

questions.korean: 나는 그가 왜 화가 났는지 이유를 알 수 없어.
answers: I can't understand the reason why he got angry.
I don't know why he got upset.

questions.korean: 더 열심히 공부했더라면 시험에 합격했을 텐데.
answers: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I'd studied more, I would have passed the test.
questions.hint: If + had + p.p., would have + p.p.
questions.explanation: 가정법 과거완료: 과거 사실과 반대되는 상상

questions.korean: 그 파티에 갔더라면 그녀를 만났을 텐데.
answers: If I had gone to the party, I would have met her.
If I'd been at the party, I could have met her.
questions.hint: If + had gone, would have met

questions.korean: 그가 그 충고를 들었더라면 실수를 피할 수 있었을 텐데.
answers: If he had listened to the advice, he could have avoided the mistake.
If he had taken the advice, he wouldn't have made that mistake.
questions.hint: If + had listened, could/would have + p.p.

questions.korean: 우산을 가져왔더라면 비에 안 젖었을 텐데.
answers: If I had brought an umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten wet.
If I'd taken my umbrella, I wouldn't have been soaked.
questions.hint: If + had brought, wouldn't have gotten wet

questions.korean: 그때 그 기회를 잡았더라면 지금 더 행복했을 텐데.
answers: If I had taken that chance, I would be happier now.
If I had seized that opportunity, I might be happier today.
questions.hint: 혼합 가정법: If + had + p.p., would + 현재
questions.explanation: 과거 조건 + 현재 결과 = 혼합 가정법

answers: She went out to get some fresh air.
She stepped outside to breathe some fresh air.

questions.korean: 나는 그 영화를 보려고 일찍 왔어.
answers: I came early to see the movie.
I arrived early in order to watch the movie.
questions.hint: to see / in order to see

questions.korean: 그는 집을 사기 위해 돈을 모으고 있어.
answers: He is saving money to buy a house.
He's been saving up money in order to buy a home.

questions.korean: 결국 그 소식을 듣게 돼서 행복했어.
answers: I was happy to hear the news.
I was glad to finally hear the news.
The book is too difficult to understand.
The book is too hard to follow.
Exercising in the morning is good for your health.
Working out in the morning is healthy.

questions.korean: 나는 새로운 언어 배우는 걸 즐겨.
answers: I enjoy learning new languages.
I love picking up new languages.
questions.explanation: pick up a language = 언어를 (자연스럽게) 배우다

answers: He avoided going to the party.
He managed to avoid attending the party.

questions.korean: 나는 TV 보는 것을 멈추고 공부했어.
answers: I stopped watching TV and studied.
I quit watching TV to study.
questions.explanation: stop to do = 하던 것을 멈추고 ~하다 (의미 다름)

questions.korean: 일찍 일어나는 것에 익숙해지는 데 시간이 걸렸어.
answers: It took time to get used to waking up early.
Getting used to waking up early took some time.
I shouldn't have said that.
I should not have said that.
questions.explanation: 과거에 한 일에 대한 후회 표현

answers: He might have left early.
He could have already left.

questions.korean: 나는 더 일찍 출발할 수 있었는데.
answers: I could have left earlier.
I could have departed sooner.
questions.hint: could have + p.p. = ~할 수 있었는데 (하지 못한 아쉬움)

questions.korean: 그녀는 그 문제를 알고 있었을 거야.
answers: She must have known about the problem.
She should have been aware of the issue.

questions.korean: 그건 더 잘 처리될 수 있었어.
answers: That could have been handled better.
It should have been dealt with better.
